{"iterations":[{"iteration_number":1,"theme":"Introduction, the state of Poljud and an analysis of the Hajduk - Dinamo derby: Hajduk's pressing and Dinamo's problems in defence, midfield and on the wings","sections":[{"subtitle":"The return of the HNL after the international break: the derby in a four-person line-up","screenshot_description":"Host Renato Špehar and three guests at the table in the studio at the start of the episode","content":"After a long international break, **Ofenziva** returns to the domestic league, and in the best possible way, with an analysis of the biggest Croatian derby between Dinamo and Hajduk. Host **Renato Špehar** announces that the episode was recorded in a line-up the channel has not had for a long time. With him are **Duje Granić**, **Luka Vujić** and **Marino Durdov**.

Špehar recalls that there was a lot of content on the channel during the break, but that now it is time for the HNL and for what interests viewers the most. Before the analysis itself, he invites them to register on the **Score HUB** app, which cooperates with Ofenziva. He describes it as a completely free version of a betting shop, that is, an opportunity to prove who predicts football results better than friends and the host's crew. Those who are the best every month can choose the jersey they want. In the Ofenziva league, all HNL and Premier League matches are predicted, and one of them was the big derby at Poljud.

**Brief match overview:**

- Dinamo took the lead with Beljo's goal.
- Hajduk equalised express-fast in the first half with an own goal by Mecena.
- Only three minutes later, at the start of the second part, Bamba brought the lead of 2:1.

Špehar immediately stresses that this was anything but a normal derby. He describes the last half hour as a complete deluge and as football in which, in the host's words, it was played in the rain without any control.","keywords":["HNL","derby","Score HUB","international break","match analysis"],"entities":["Ofenziva","Renato Špehar","Duje Granić","Luka Vujić","Marino Durdov","Score HUB","Dinamo","Hajduk","Poljud","Premier League"]},{"subtitle":"A covered stadium that leaks: Granić on the day at Poljud","screenshot_description":"Duje Granić describes the experience from Poljud and journalists holding umbrellas over laptops","content":"Špehar first turns to **Duje Granić**, who followed the derby live, ironically noting that he was under a roof, but only in theory. Granić confirms that the roof almost did not exist. The derby, he says, went to two extremes.

On one side stands a positive picture: a fun day at the stadium, a turnaround for the home team and a good atmosphere. On the other side, the journalists in their box could not work on laptops because rain was falling on their equipment at a supposedly covered stadium. They had to run away and hold umbrellas in order to do basic jobs. Špehar adds that he has a photo from the press box in which one can see how soaked the notebooks are. Photos also circulated on Instagram, and the place was described as leaking for all media workers.

About the play in the last twenty or so minutes Granić speaks vividly. He compares that football to that Christmas match of the English and the Germans in the First World War. With Ofenziva colleague **Marko Štrkalj** he concluded that the whole experience was fun. Still, when one looks at the whole, the pitch can get soaked because the rain was truly heavy. Poljud's infrastructure problems, which are talked about a lot and should continue to be talked about, are not acceptable, especially not in the 2010s and later, when such things repeat.","keywords":["Poljud","rain","press box","infrastructure","covered stadium"],"entities":["Poljud","Duje Granić","Marko Štrkalj","Ofenziva","Instagram"]},{"subtitle":"Renovation or a new stadium: Vujić holds that Poljud is dilapidated","screenshot_description":"Luka Vujić explains why Hajduk needs a new stadium","content":"Špehar opens a topic that has been very current in the media in recent days. After the presentation of the new Maksimir project, Split also activated itself, so Hajduk's fans and the club want a new stadium. Prime Minister **Andrej Plenković** announced a reconstruction. The host asks whether the match can be seen as a vintage derby that will be remembered or as one more bad image of the league in the world.

**Luka Vujić** holds that the downpour fell at an ideal moment: just when the topic is current, it showed why it is current. He admits that Split probably does not need two new stadiums, especially since Spaladium arena was badly managed and was not commercially exploited. But Split, and especially Hajduk, really needs a new stadium. As examples of dilapidation he cites:

- a roof that leaks, in a dilapidated state,
- stairs in the press box and in the stands that are collapsing, so people put a piece of board under them to support them,
- the shaking of the scaffolding under their feet at the match in Osijek, when it seemed it would collapse at any moment,
- a load-bearing pillar that two years ago, as Vujić remembers, was tied with copper wire.

Vujić thinks that a renovation would be just make-up. Apart from the dressing rooms and the pitch, almost everything would need to be changed, so there is no sense in investing in such moves. He admits that the problem is that Hajduk must play somewhere in the meantime, and as an option he mentions renovating Park mladeži, which is expensive but necessary given how long Poljud has been neglected.

The argument that Poljud is cultural property, according to Vujić, does not hold water because it became that a little over ten years ago only so that money for a renovation could be extracted from the European Union, which was then not properly carried out. Poljud, he thinks, is dearer to those who do not go to the stadium than to those who actually use it. He recalls that the English demolished much bigger stadiums too, such as Highbury and the old Wembley, and that a stadium is a consumable. Hajduk needs a new stadium, at Poljud or somewhere else. It is not clear to him what the use of the old Poljud would be, except for athletics, and commercially he does not see concerts being profitable.

Špehar concludes with a contrast: everyone saw at the national team matches how nice it is when the weather is nice and the stadium is full, and such situations show how bad the infrastructure is.","keywords":["new stadium","Poljud","cultural property","renovation","Park mladeži"],"entities":["Poljud","Maksimir","Split","Hajduk","Andrej Plenković","Spaladium arena","Park mladeži","Osijek","European Union","Highbury","Wembley"]},{"subtitle":"A fun derby or a bad image of the league? Durdov relativizes","screenshot_description":"Marino Durdov answers the question of whether the derby was fun","content":"To the question of whether the derby was ultra fun or sent a bad image of the league, **Marino Durdov** answers that it is a relative concept to him, because among us it is often presumed what a fun derby is. Objectively, he says, the match may not have been so interesting to someone who wants to watch quality football. Still, when one looks back five-six years, a good part of the derbies was a bigger puddle, and in better conditions, because of the styles of play and everything else.

Watching the recording, Durdov says he was not bored. Until the sixtieth minute he had something to watch at every moment. After that there was a lot of bickering and empty runs. As for content, that is the football itself, he assesses that there was nothing special.","keywords":["derby","fun football","league quality","styles of play"],"entities":["Marino Durdov","Dinamo","Hajduk"]},{"subtitle":"How Hajduk stopped Dinamo: high pressing and a compressed middle","screenshot_description":"Marino Durdov analyses Hajduk's high pressing on Dinamo's back line","content":"Špehar moves on to the analysis for which the episode was recorded and asks Durdov how, in his opinion, Hajduk stopped Dinamo. Durdov liked Hajduk's approach most at the start of the play in the second half, when the team came out high and pressed excellently.

He describes Hajduk's pressing as, at moments, so aggressive that it would be silly to say frenzied, but very active. Dinamo was thereby put into panic and could not get out of its back line. The cause was not only the high pressure on the defence but also the middle of the pitch, where Hajduk, through work and morale, created a compressed space. According to Durdov, it was not perfect, but in moments of panic it was good enough to create problems for the opponent.

The tactical analysis, he adds, partly fell through after the deluge, when the match turned into real chaos, so it is hard to talk about tactics and set-up. He sees Hajduk's greatest advantage in the fact that this season, including in this match, it gradually rises and builds through the game. Mistakes in a series constantly exist, but they do not constrain the team so much that it loses continuity. Dinamo, on the contrary, after conceding a goal was in decline.","keywords":["high pressing","back line","compressed middle","panic","continuity"],"entities":["Hajduk","Dinamo","Marino Durdov","Renato Špehar"]},{"subtitle":"Communication and concentration: problems shared by both teams","screenshot_description":"Durdov on screen explains the throw-in situation and the first goal","content":"Durdov warns that both teams had problems with communication and concentration. According to his view, players often duplicate each other on the wings or in the middle when they should not, and two take over the same task, while nobody shouts to anyone else and helps.

As an example he cites the situation before Hajduk's goal after Dinamo's throw-in. Three Hajduk players watched the taker of the throw-in, and one ran out behind their backs and received the ball. When he played the return ball, **Marušić** came out and extricated himself from the situation only with a short escape. Most people rightly criticised the goalkeeper, who also went who knows where. For Durdov it is nevertheless an example of a series of events that can be called a question of concentration, but primarily they show that there is no loud communication and help on the pitch. He admits that this match did not cost Hajduk points, but the problems are visible.

Špehar stresses that this is about play without the ball, which in Croatia needs to be constantly emphasised and encouraged because it is not innate to our teams.","keywords":["communication","concentration","play without the ball","throw-in","first goal"],"entities":["Marušić","Hajduk","Dinamo","Marino Durdov"]},{"subtitle":"Granić: Hajduk showed character, and Garcia got what he asked for","screenshot_description":"Duje Granić next to a tactical display of Hajduk's pressing with the wingers and full-backs","content":"Špehar invites **Duje Granić** to comment on Hajduk's brave ideas and the shown pressing situation. Granić explains that it is the way in which Hajduk presses the whole season: the winger goes out onto the centre-back, and the full-back must support that pressure. This season, he claims, it has functioned very well, and in the derby too it showed incredible intensity in all phases. When the winger and the full-back do not support each other, the opponent finds space. Here Hajduk, on the contrary, had constant movements and mutual support in the pressure.

He notes that Hajduk went in with high risk in the upper part of the pressure and that errors in communication nevertheless existed, especially at the goal. But Dinamo, which was chasing the result, did not have periods of domination or control of the match, as might be expected. Practically the whole match it did not lead, except for a minute or two between the two goals.

Granić then speaks about coach **Garcia**. He thinks it was not a tactically spectacular match and recalls Hajduk's last-season defeats in derbies, including his first podcast after the 2:0 defeat at Poljud, when he assessed that Hajduk had played the match tactically well. The difference in the coaching part of the job, he says, is not excessive. That is why he likes Garcia's statement that it is better to play as a team and play badly than to play well and not play as a team.

In key moments, when chaos arises, Hajduk did not fall apart but reacted and made a turnaround against Dinamo. Granić assesses this as impressive and more valuable than some big tactical adjustment. Such wholeness, he concludes, the team shows most in the phase of defence.","keywords":["Garcia","pressing","team character","turnaround","phase of defence"],"entities":["Duje Granić","Garcia","Hajduk","Dinamo","Poljud"]},{"subtitle":"Two sixes finally at Hajduk: how the midfield got shape","screenshot_description":"Luka Vujić praises Hajduk's rear midfield and Del Moral","content":"Špehar recalls the previous derby at Poljud, when Hajduk's rear midfielders were **Williamson** and **Skoko**. Hajduk then entered the pressing well, but was not physically strong enough, so Dinamo outplayed the pressing and scored a goal. This time Hajduk came out onto the pitch with a real six and a real eight: **Del Moral** controls the defensive spaces well, and his partner is technically powerful and masterful on the ball. It seemed that this was the main change compared to the previous derbies, and in circumstances when another important player was missing.

**Luka Vujić** follows on: neither Hajduk nor Dinamo changed substantially tactically. Dinamo pressed slightly differently, for example at Hajduk's goal from the throw-in, where Zec was closer and Badelj jumped out. What decided it were the profiles of the players. Hajduk's new midfielder pleased Vujić as soon as he came and he thinks that at the end of the year he will be among the better reinforcements of the transfer window. He praises him for:

- good play on the ball,
- quick control and passing from the first touch, so he does not slow the game down,
- good running.

Del Moral was, according to Vujić, along with Bamba and Hrgović among the best in the match. He is not technically so skilled in the final third, but his running was very valuable, and in defence he is considerably better than the previous options, who have problems in the phase of defence and in reading the game. The player who played that position before, he stresses, poorly recognises when to go out forward, while Del Moral in a duel takes both the player and the ball. Vujić hopes that the player who was missing will also return, with at least 80 percent of his abilities, because that would give additional progress in defence.

Vujić concludes that Hajduk finally has something that has been chronically lacking for years, aggression in the rear midfield, which was missing for Garcia and for the previous coach. Špehar confirms this: with two sixes it is much easier to put a profile together, and the midfield was for a long time the weakness of the whole roster, not only the coach's decision.","keywords":["midfield line","rear midfielders","Del Moral","reinforcements","six"],"entities":["Del Moral","Williamson","Skoko","Zec","Badelj","Bamba","Hrgović","Garcia","Hajduk","Dinamo","Poljud","Luka Vujić"]},{"subtitle":"The centre-back dossier: risks, advantages and what they will play in Europe","screenshot_description":"Duje Granić and Luka Vujić discuss Hajduk's centre-backs","content":"Špehar then returns to the centre-back who before the goal left Beljo and had a risky tackle on one Dinamo player that could easily have ended in a red card. He recalls that this repeats: a big mistake, then a good match after it, as well as cardinal mistakes in past matches and a problematic build-up of attack. He asks whether what this player offers tactically can justify everything that happens in the other phases of the game.

**Duje Granić** describes him as a wild card player. You know what you can get, but you never know to which side he will go. He likes him for his aggressiveness, physical strength, good passing and dribbling, but all of it is unbridled. There are matches, like the one against Rakov, when he is among the better ones and lifts the defence, but then Rijeka and Dinamo come. Granić admits that, had the match stayed 0:1, they would again be talking about the negative context, but asks whether Hajduk has a better solution. He is interested in what will happen when Hadžić or Madunić returns, who could be defensively more powerful for matches like the one with Ajax. He notes that with both centre-backs Hajduk takes on a big risk because of the way they play. At this moment that centre-back is, for him, the first left centre-back, and when Hurem, the full-back, is not in play, it pays to live with his mistakes, especially in the HNL, because he is physically more powerful and faster than the competition.

**Luka Vujić** has a sharper stance. Against Ajax he expects Hajduk to defend deeper and that **Hadžić** will come into the game ahead of him, and **Marić** (as Vujić names him) could be shifted to left centre-back because he is very good there, as he played in Istra. He thinks Hajduk missed a little with one centre-back reinforcement of the summer, whom he holds to be the weakest of all. One centre-back has his best match against Rakov because that team plays long balls and hoofing, but Vujić thinks he messes up too much, likes to go forward and unnecessarily stirs up trouble. He has physical predispositions, but in reading the game he has not progressed in a year.

Vujić nevertheless sees a reason why that centre-back could stay in the first line-up in the HNL: Hajduk is more in the opponent's half, the last line stands high, and he is the only one of the centre-backs who can reliably cover depth over a wide space. **Kalinić** is calmer in positioning and jumping, but is much slower. In Europe, against stronger opponents, Hajduk will drop lower, so this centre-back could end up on the bench. Vujić notes that Hajduk could lack one more faster centre-back who covers depth, because the three current ones have practically the same flaw. Whether the club will react here depends on finances in the winter transfer window.","keywords":["centre-backs","wild card","covering depth","risk","Europe"],"entities":["Hajduk","Dinamo","Rijeka","Rakov","Ajax","Hadžić","Madunić","Marić","Kalinić","Hurem","Istra","Duje Granić","Luka Vujić"]},{"subtitle":"Dinamo's right-back and the deeper problems of the Zagreb team","screenshot_description":"Marino Durdov explains the problems of Dinamo's right side","content":"Špehar asks Durdov whether the biggest surprise was Dinamo's right side, that is, the right-back who did not respond to Hrgović's challenge. Both goals, namely, fell from that side. He also asks whether Dinamo has deeper problems.

Durdov says there are certainly deeper problems. When it comes to the full-back, he recalls that Kovačić said after the match that the player was fine and was not worse than the rest of the team. Durdov agrees, but stresses: if that is a fact, it means that the others were very bad. The player came to Dinamo as a rotation full-back, for patching in Europe or the cup, and was also mentioned as a player for the B team. He had no big mistakes, but he is a type of player with a grade of 6.0 – 6.5, with whom one always knows what one is getting. He limits the team, especially going forward. He is physically strong and can run in a straight line, but does not have the personality of a modern full-back.

On that side ahead of him was **Lisica**, also a very limited player who needs depth and space for crossing into the corridor. Today those corridors were not there, so the attacker switched off completely on the right side and the team was left at the mercy of the defence. According to Durdov, the side was targeted with reason and with reason most actions went towards it.

While **Valentić** is healthy, but not yet in form, **Galešić** has already been tried at right-back, and Durdov thinks it makes no sense that after everything he steps in from the start in the derby. He concludes that some problems impose themselves as permanent: the transfer window was not carried out perfectly and every profile in the squad is not what was needed. Still, even with the existing options at least one match could have been played without repeated mistakes.","keywords":["right-back","Dinamo","rotation","limited players","transfer window"],"entities":["Dinamo","Hajduk","Hrgović","Lisica","Valentić","Galešić","Kovačić","Marino Durdov"]},{"subtitle":"Vujić: full-backs, wings and a squad that does not reach the investments","screenshot_description":"Luka Vujić talks about Dinamo's full-backs and wingers","content":"Špehar asks Luka Vujić whether this is a problem of Dinamo's squad, which repeats through several matches. Lokomotiva and Gorica sought a point at Maksimir until the end, there was the defeat in Osijek and a barren performance in Europe. He asks whether the team is simply poorly put together.

Vujić thinks it is a mixture of both. Dinamo last year also had a similar problem of insecurity in itself, and coach Kovačić then did not even come out to media conferences. Part of the chaos comes from saving on the reserve full-backs: a player was brought in who is, at best, an average HNL full-back. Dinamo would otherwise, for the best full-back, bring in a replacement from a powerful club, and here that is not the case. Such a player, says Vujić, would play well at the level of Vukovar, and from Dinamo a level higher is expected.

Vujić adds that Hajduk also did not exploit that side as much as it could. **Hrgović** gave width and sent a couple of good crosses, but he is not penetrating in one-on-one situations. Hajduk created more problems through Bamba on the right side. Dinamo is unconvincing in defence this year, and Vujić assumes that one of the reasons why **Šutić** drifted more into the left half-space was that he attacked the space between two Dinamo defenders. Before the goal for 2:1 Bamba passed quite easily on that side. Vujić agrees that Galešić should start at least as a centre-back or right-back, because he shows the most of all this season.

The wing positions also leave question marks. **Rodriguez** is only now getting into the game and it is not clear what can be expected of him, and Almeida is kept on the left wing although he is drawn to the middle of the pitch and seems more natural from the right side. Dinamo in recent years was most successful precisely through the wings, but Oršić is not like in the first period at Dinamo and can hardly make a difference. Similar to Europe last year, Dinamo has no player who makes a difference in the final third. Stojković partly solved that in the second part of last season, but now, when he is injured, there is not him either.

Vujić concludes that Dinamo definitely can do better, but he does not believe it can do significantly better with the existing squad, although a lot of money was invested. Špehar recalls that at the end of last season the team looked organised, and now Dinamo, although without Mišić and Stojković, practically until the panicky attack in stoppage time did not create more than one big chance.","keywords":["Dinamo","full-backs","wings","squad","investments"],"entities":["Dinamo","Kovačić","Hrgović","Šutić","Rodriguez","Almeida","Oršić","Stojković","Galešić","Lokomotiva","Gorica","Osijek","Maksimir","Vukovar","Luka Vujić"]},{"subtitle":"Granić: without Mišić and Stojković Dinamo's midfield lost its balance","screenshot_description":"Duje Granić explains the importance of Mišić and Stojković in Dinamo's midfield","content":"To Špehar's question of how it came about that Dinamo created only one big chance, **Duje Granić** answers that everything comes down to the midfield. In the best moments of last season the midfield with **Mišić** and **Stojković** was perfectly balanced. Mišić is a creator at the bottom, who does a bit of everything and everything excellently, and Stojković brings energy, but is more a ten than an eight.

This time that was not there. The player who replaced Mišić has his qualities, but, says Granić, nobody in this league is Mišić, so it was not possible to play through him. Even when the ball would reach him, Hajduk closed that position well, and one cannot expect from him such a range of passing and creation. **Kačavenda** is unquestionably a player whom many coaches would want in the team because he can be put in several positions, is always energetic and can play box to box. In pure attacking play he is nevertheless quite limited compared to Stojković.

Granić also adds the fact that Dinamo lost the wings: it was an underrated player who gave a lot, and Dinamo's wings in the last matches do not give goals. Goals come down to set pieces and Beljo, and there is no longer a top scorer from the wing. From **Oršić** the level that the club wanted was not obtained. With the absence of Mišić and Stojković, **Zaić**, whom Granić last season highlighted as a player who can do everything, is weaker this season.

All of this, he concludes, gives a whole that cannot function at the previous level. In the current line-up it is not known who does what, which was a completely different picture from the spring, when the team trampled everything in front of it, especially after Europe.","keywords":["midfield line","Mišić","Stojković","team balance","absence of key players"],"entities":["Duje Granić","Mišić","Stojković","Kačavenda","Oršić","Zaić","Beljo","Dinamo","Hajduk"]},{"subtitle":"Dinamo's offensive options: can wing football bring the edge?","screenshot_description":"Marino Durdov analyses Dinamo's offensive options and the role of the wings","content":"Špehar assumes that with the return of Mišić and Stojković the midfield will return to normal, but asks Durdov how he sees the offensive options. He is especially interested in the role of **Ivanišević**, who should be the decisive edge in matches like this one and in the rest of the HNL, and in the other players on the wings and in attack, who apart from desire show no quality for now.

Durdov says that Ivanišević is currently not in form, but is capable of making a difference and changing the gravity in attack. He is primarily a vertical player: he will probably play mostly on the left, but will drift into the half-space, look for a shot and quick combination play, which is what Dinamo lacks the most.

The absence of Mišić is felt the most, explains Durdov, because he connects both wings and is capable of quickly switching the centre of gravity of play from one side to the other. This is especially important when the wings are in poor form or do not fit the profile, so constant movement is needed in order to open a hole in the defence. Several previous matches showed that without him it is not enough. One should also see how Rodriguez will show up when he gets more minutes.

Durdov thinks that players who cut into the middle and look for the half-space suit Dinamo. He thinks it is proven that play with classic wingers brings nothing, because each of them is limited in some part. **Hodža**, **Lisica** and possibly **Oršić** would suit most for European matches. If something lastingly effective is to be achieved when Dinamo is a team with possession, these are **Ivanišević** and similar types of players who, with their technique, instinct for goal and creation, will create the decisive edge. Špehar agrees and announces that this will be the biggest challenge for coach Kovačić in a period that brings many challenges.","keywords":["offensive options","wings","half-space","Ivanišević","creation"],"entities":["Marino Durdov","Ivanišević","Mišić","Stojković","Rodriguez","Hodža","Lisica","Oršić","Dinamo","HNL","Kovačić"]}]},{"iteration_number":2,"theme":"Hajduk's individuals, the assessment of the refereeing and a preview of Hajduk's and Dinamo's European matches","sections":[{"subtitle":"Transition to Hajduk's heroes: Bamba, man of the match, from „summer” to „evergreen” winger?","screenshot_description":"Host Renato Špehar shows on screen Bamba's statistics as man of the match: goal, dribbles and created chances","content":"After Marino Durdov concluded that the biggest challenge for Dinamo's coach will be finding creativity in attack, **Renato Špehar** switches the topic to Hajduk's individuals. First in line is Bamba, whom Ofenziva chose as man of the match.

Špehar states numbers that support this:

- **one goal**,
- **six successful dribbles out of seven attempted**,
- **two created big chances**,
- **seven accurate passes out of nine**.

The host also recalls the irony that the same player, about whom **Duje Granić** after one of the earlier matches said he would no longer like to see him at Hajduk, has now become phenomenal. To Luka Vujić he poses the question of whether Bamba is actually much better than is thought of him when he has an organised midfield behind him and can do what his job is: be unpredictable and play one on one.

**Luka Vujić** answers that Bamba is, in his opinion, absolutely the same player as when he arrived at Hajduk. Only the way he is used changes. Vujić speaks about the „famous summer Bamba”: at the start of the season he would get continuity of matches, later he would end up on the bench and would hardly return to rhythm. Bamba is a player who lives on continuity and is best when he plays regularly. Now he has played all nine rounds for Hajduk and, Vujić thinks, has finally got the role that suits him under Garcia. He also recalls that coach Garcia has always extracted the maximum from wingers in his career, which was seen already in Istra.

Bamba's virtues Vujić sees in big matches: **he attacks the empty space behind the last line, is the fastest player in the team and was excellent in receiving long balls**. Defence is the weaker part of his game and in the final third he can make mistakes, so he will never be a winger worth 10 or 20 million euros. But when he gets enough space, he is fast and straight-line and can bring a lot. Hajduk paid **750 thousand euros** for him and Vujić thinks he is worth that when put in the right context. He should not be put into excessive combination play, where he drops for the ball, because then there will be no use from him.

Vujić also thinks that Bamba is better in defence than before. It helps him that the right-back behind him defends better, and Del Moral as the right six can jump out and cover the space if the ball is lost. He concludes that this is the moment for him to stop being just the summer Bamba and become the „green Bamba”, a winger for all seasons, and that this is his best season so far. He believes that in Europe, including against Ajax, he will be one of the triggers for going forward because he can be targeted with long balls in depth.

Špehar adds that it is often forgotten that players are people with their characteristics. Coach Garcia said of Bamba that he is very sensitive and needs continuity. At one point the question was Bamba or Šutalo, and now Bamba has taken over the position and, considering the competition, will hold it at least until winter.","keywords":["Bamba","continuity","play in depth","big matches","summer Bamba"],"entities":["Hajduk","Dinamo","Garcia","Istra","Ajax","Del Moral","Šutalo"]},{"subtitle":"Granić on Bamba's unpredictability: from matches when you cannot stand him to a winger for every important match","screenshot_description":"Duje Granić talks about Bamba's extremes and coach Garcia's trust in him","content":"**Duje Granić** follows on from Vujić and confirms that Bamba is the same player as when he arrived. The difference is in the use and in the momentum that continuity creates for him. Granić also stresses what Garcia said: Bamba is sensitive and the slightest falling out of rhythm demotes him into a player whom it is impossible to watch. According to Granić, no Hajduk player in the last few years has gone from one extreme to the other like him, from ten matches in which he is excellent to ten in which you cannot wait for him to leave the game.
